_why: A/B of the burn's annotate model (tools/puzzle_worker.sh via ANNOTATE_MODEL/ANNOTATE_EFFORT): the next 20 keyed puzzles in burn queue order, each run three ways through the burn's Annotate path (worker_annotate + worker_finish, commit stubbed) in scratch clones. eq_tokens weights in 1, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1, out 5 (the burn token analysis's quota weights, same for both models); usd uses list prices Opus $5/$25, Sonnet $3/$15 per M. A check passes first time when its summary has no ERROR; spotless = no warnings either. Blind judge: 10 clues, labels shuffled, judged against cryptic-hint-rungs-no-giveaways + cryptic-surface-is-a-joke; rank points 2/1/0 per clue.

blind_note: Two independent Opus judges, same pack of 10 clues newly annotated in all three arms (one per puzzle). Both judges flagged definitionFit naming the answer in most versions of every arm, so the giveaway counts do not separate the arms. Blog checks compared 481 clue facts per arm with 0 disagreements: annotate_check already enforces blog agreement, so it cannot discriminate. All 20 puzzles were keyed (no cold solve fits the time box), so answer accuracy is 0 changed answers in every arm by construction.

round2_opus_med_vs_low._why: Paul 10-12: 'saving 12% seems good, did low effort did as good of a job?' Round 1's 10-clue judging was too small. Same harness (worker_annotate + worker_finish, commit stubbed, scratch clones), Opus medium vs Opus low only, on 40 fresh burn-queue puzzles (15 series, max 3 each, keyed, >=5 unannotated clues, none of round 1's 20), 2 runs at a time per arm. A usage limit cut both arms mid-run; the 4 runs that had done real work were resumed (--resume, same session; tokens from the merged transcript), the ~50 refused within 16s with no work were rerun fresh. cyclops-321 dropped (its model answers were reopened for solving in both arms). Weights as round 1. Blind judging: 2 clues per paired puzzle, A/B shuffled per clue, 2 independent Opus judges (better of two + margin, wrong parse, giveaway) against cryptic-hint-rungs-no-giveaways + cryptic-surface-is-a-joke; a third Opus judge on clues where they disagreed on the better version or on wrong parses. Winner = the two judges' shared pick, else the third judge's. sign_test_p is two-sided on winners. prose = objective fullness of every newly annotated clue in paired puzzles.
round2_opus_med_vs_low.verdict: keep medium: low saves 14% eq tokens per clue but loses the blind judging 8-34 (sign test p=7e-5; easy 2-20, hard 6-14), writes a walkthrough on 46% of clues vs 70%, passes the first check on 16/38 vs 23/38, and has 3 majority wrong parses vs 1 plus one unshipped puzzle (book-16012). Not within noise.
